text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms Hazel Poa –   5 To ask the Minister for Health (a) what is the result of the investigation into the case involving an expectant mother losing her child after being left unattended for a long time at the emergency department of the National University Hospital (NUH); (b) whether there are any previous similar cases; and (c) what steps will be taken to prevent future recurrence and to address the wider problem of overload situation at hospitals’ emergency departments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It was with a heavy heart that I read about the unfortunate incident that happened at National University Hospital (NUH) two weeks ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The family had put up a social media post recently acknowledging this and further acknowledged that the mother had not been left unattended for two hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Indeed, she received attention and care from the NUH Emergency Department (ED) team from the time that she arrived.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They further noted that the sad and unfortunate outcome of the pregnancy was not the result of her experience at the hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Out of respect for the couple's request for privacy and confidentiality reasons, I will not go into details of the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: COVID-19 has resulted in the public hospitals' EDs facing very high demands and our healthcare workers have been working continuously to attend to all patients with COVID-19 and those with non-COVID-19 conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: All patients will be triaged based on presenting history, symptoms and clinical parameters so that those with life-threatening conditions are prioritised.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Singaporean couple at the heart of the matter are, actually, residents of Zhenghua.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As their Member of Parliament, I have communicated with them on several occasions and having to cremate one's child is an emotional journey for any parent.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The father told me that it was never his intention to cast any blame on the hospital or the healthcare workers when he posted on social media.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: His intention was to really seek answers for the two hours of wait time that he and his wife experienced at the A&E.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It was so because he was unable to seek answers or any response over a period of five days and this included the time when his wife was being treated at a high dependency ward.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He finally got a response from a patient care officer when his post went viral.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, following this incident and with the objective of improving protocols, would MOH be assessing how hospitals should improve the provision of critical information to patients in a timely manner with empathy?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do believe that greater transparency will strengthen the trust that Singaporeans already have in our healthcare institutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And this process review was done in consultation with MOH and the Director of Medical Services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The lessons will be learnt and shared across our healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Janil Puthucheary, you mentioned about the question raised by Ms Ng Ling Ling earlier.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Which question is that, for our record purposes?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My concern is really for the healthcare workers who were involved in this unfortunate incident, because when this news went viral, clearly, they were the first in line to be blamed.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My question is: how could we better protect them in the future when these things happen again?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Because, apparently, it was not the first; there was a subsequent incident where healthcare workers were blamed.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What can we do to protect them in the future in this regard?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Adverse incidents will happen in these complex, high-risk and high-intensity situations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And when they do, everybody feels bad, it is a tragic outcome from an emotive empathy point of view.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Anybody hearing about it feels lost, feels sympathy.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The processes to investigate and follow up on incidents, such as these, are well-known to our healthcare system and healthcare staff.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At root, however, it would be helpful if, when allegations and incidents are raised, that these are based on facts rather than speculation.
